# Foundry — complete documentation

Source: https://foundry.insightdevhub.ro/


---

# Installation

> Download the Foundry archive, copy the classes you need into your project and load them with require_once, an SPL autoloader or Composer PSR-4.

Canonical: https://foundry.insightdevhub.ro/docs/installation/

Foundry is not installed with a package manager. Every class is a single, self-contained PHP file: you copy the files you need into your project, and they become part of your code base. There is no vendor tree to update and no third-party code to audit.

## Download {#download}

The archive contains the 51 classes as PHP 8.3 source files, in a single `foundry/` folder.

<p><a class="btn btn-primary" href="/downloads/foundry-php83.zip" download>Download foundry-php83.zip</a> <span class="muted">249 KB</span></p>

SHA-256 checksum: `e6bbcbeb8cfe1f742e3537243f1f345ff7cfa926eaa468866725280ddc065d87`

Verify the archive after downloading it:

```bash
sha256sum foundry-php83.zip                         # Linux
shasum -a 256 foundry-php83.zip                     # macOS
```

```powershell
Get-FileHash .\foundry-php83.zip -Algorithm SHA256   # Windows
```

## Copy the files

Copy only the classes you need into a dedicated folder of your project, for example `lib/Utilities/` (or `src/Utilities/` if your project already uses `src/`). The classes do not depend on each other, so any subset works.

```text
your-project/
├── lib/
│   └── Utilities/
│       ├── Json.php
│       ├── Validator.php
│       └── Csv.php
└── public/
    └── index.php
```

## Loading the classes

All classes live in the `Foundry` namespace. Pick one of the three approaches below.

### With require_once

The simplest option: one line per class you use.

```php
require_once __DIR__.'/lib/Utilities/Json.php';

use Foundry\Json;

$data = Json::decode($body);
```

### With an SPL autoloader

Register the autoloader once, in your application bootstrap file. Classes are then loaded the first time they are used.

```php
spl_autoload_register(static function (string $class): void {
    $prefix = 'Foundry\\';
    if (strncmp($class, $prefix, strlen($prefix)) === 0) {      // also works on PHP 7.4
        require __DIR__.'/lib/Utilities/'.substr($class, strlen($prefix)).'.php';
    }
});
```

### With Composer

If your project already uses Composer, map the namespace in your own `composer.json`, then run `composer dump-autoload`:

```json
"autoload": {
    "psr-4": { "Foundry\\": "lib/Utilities/" },
    "files": ["lib/Utilities/Str.php", "lib/Utilities/Debug.php"]
}
```

> **Note:** The `files` entries are only needed if you use the global helper functions `e()` (defined in `Str.php`) or `dump()` / `dd()` (defined in `Debug.php`). An autoloader loads a file only when its class is first referenced, so functions called before that would not exist yet.

## PHP extensions

Some classes need PHP extensions. Check what your server has with `php -m`. The table below is generated from the source code of each class.

| Extension | Required by |
| --- | --- |
| `mbstring` | `Encoding`, `Upload`, `Str`, `Validator`, `Paginator`, `Csv`, `Xlsx`, `Xml`, `Mailer`, `Request`, `Response`, `View`, `Breadcrumbs`, `Flash`, `Debug` |
| `fileinfo` | `File`, `Upload`, `Mailer` |
| `session` | `Session`, `Csrf`, `Flash` |
| `iconv` | `Encoding`, `Csv` |
| `openssl` | `Crypt`, `Mailer` |
| `xmlreader` | `Xlsx`, `Xml` |
| `xmlwriter` | `Xlsx`, `Xml` |
| `zip` | `Zip`, `Xlsx` |
| `bcmath` | `Money` |
| `curl` | `HttpClient` |
| `dom` | `Xml` |
| `gd` | `Image` |
| `oci8` | `Oracle` |
| `pdo_mysql` | `MySQL` |
| `pdo_sqlite` | `SQLite` |
| `simplexml` | `Xml` |

Classes not listed above run on a default PHP installation. Each class page also lists its requirements at the top.

## Updating

When a class changes, replace its file with the newer version. Every file has a `@version` tag in its header, so version differences are visible at a glance, and every class page in this documentation shows the current version.

> **Warning:** Do not edit copied files directly. A fix made in one project is lost the next time the file is replaced. Report the problem instead, so the fix lands in the library for every project.

---

# Usage and exceptions

> How Foundry classes are called, which exceptions they throw, how error messages are written, and when to catch them.

Canonical: https://foundry.insightdevhub.ro/docs/usage/

## Calling the classes

All classes live in the `Foundry` namespace. Most utilities are static (`Json`, `Str`, `Cast`, `Date`, `Money`); stateful ones are objects you create (`Validator`, `Log`, `MySQL`, `View`). Each file header documents the purpose and rules of the class, and every public method has a docblock listing what it throws. The same information appears on the reference page of each class.

```php
use Foundry\Cast;
use Foundry\Date;
use Foundry\Money;

$id = Cast::toInt($_GET['id'] ?? null);        // '12' -> 12; 'abc', '' or missing -> exception
$date = Date::parse('15.03.2026', 'd.m.Y');    // 31.02.2026 -> exception, never rolled over to 03.03.2026
$total = Money::add('1250.50', '99.99');       // '1350.49', without floating-point inaccuracies
```

## Exceptions

Foundry never signals an error by returning `false` or `null`. Every failure throws one of the standard PHP SPL exceptions. There are no custom exception classes to learn or import.

| Exception | Typical meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `InvalidArgumentException` | A parameter is wrong: a negative depth, an unknown option, an invalid rule. Usually a bug in the calling code. |
| `UnexpectedValueException` | The data is wrong: a value that is not an integer, a date that does not exist, a malformed amount. Usually user input. |
| `RuntimeException` | The environment failed: a file cannot be written, a connection was refused, a command timed out. |
| `LogicException` | An operation was called in the wrong state, for example using a session that was not started. |
| `JsonException` | Invalid JSON, invalid UTF-8, or a value that cannot be encoded. |

The exact exceptions of every method are listed under **Throws** in its reference entry.

## Error messages

Messages follow one pattern, so a log line tells you what failed and where without a debugger:

```text
<Class>::<method>(): <what happened> [<context>]: <root cause>.
```

```text
Json::decode(): Syntax error (input length: 24 bytes).
```

Messages never contain the data being processed. They report its type, length or path instead, so logs stay free of personal data such as names, CNP numbers, IBANs or passwords.

Native PHP warnings (from `fopen()`, `unserialize()`, `gzdecode()` and others) are captured inside the class and become the cause of the exception. The `@` error suppression operator is never used, and warnings never reach your global error handler.

## When to catch

You do not need `try` / `catch` blocks everywhere. Unhandled exceptions bubble up to `ErrorHandler`, which logs them and returns a generic HTTP 500 page (see [Application bootstrap](https://foundry.insightdevhub.ro/docs/bootstrap/)). Catch only what you can actually recover from, typically invalid user input:

```php
use Foundry\Number;

try {
    $amount = Number::parse($_POST['amount']);        // '1.234,50' -> 1234.5
} catch (UnexpectedValueException $e) {
    $errors['amount'] = 'The amount is invalid.';
}
```

For whole forms, use `Validator` instead of catching per field: it collects one error per field without throwing. See [Form handling](https://foundry.insightdevhub.ro/docs/form-handling/).

---

# Application bootstrap

> The few lines to run once in your entry point - environment, logging, error handling, security headers and sessions.

Canonical: https://foundry.insightdevhub.ro/docs/bootstrap/

Including a Foundry file never changes global state. Classes that do change it (`ErrorHandler`, `Session`, `SecurityHeaders`) only act when you call them explicitly, once, at the start of each request.

## A typical entry point

```php
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

require __DIR__.'/../bootstrap/autoload.php';    // require_once lines or the SPL autoloader

use Foundry\Env;
use Foundry\ErrorHandler;
use Foundry\Log;
use Foundry\SecurityHeaders;
use Foundry\Session;

Env::load(__DIR__.'/../.env');
Env::required('DB_HOST', 'DB_DATABASE', 'DB_USERNAME', 'DB_PASSWORD');

$log = new Log(__DIR__.'/../storage/logs/app.log', minLevel: 'info', daily: true, maxFiles: 30);

ErrorHandler::register(
    debug: Env::bool('APP_DEBUG', false),             // true only in local development
    logger: fn (Throwable $e) => $log->error('Uncaught exception', ['exception' => $e]),
);
SecurityHeaders::send();
Session::start(['name' => 'APPSESSID', 'idleTimeout' => 1800]);
```

## What each step does

1. `Env::load()` reads the `.env` file (phpdotenv syntax) and `Env::required()` fails immediately if a variable is missing, instead of failing later on first use.
2. `Log` writes PSR-3 levels with a JSON context, masks sensitive keys and rotates files daily, keeping the last 30.
3. `ErrorHandler::register()` converts PHP warnings into `ErrorException`, logs deprecations, and turns uncaught exceptions and fatal errors into a logged, generic HTTP 500 response. Stack traces are shown only when `debug` is true.
4. `SecurityHeaders::send()` sends a Content-Security-Policy with a per-request nonce, HSTS on HTTPS, and the other defensive headers.
5. `Session::start()` starts the session with hardened cookie options and clears it after 30 minutes of inactivity.

> **Tip:** Keep `debug: false` in production. Detailed traces can expose file paths and configuration values to visitors.

## Development helpers

`Debug` is disabled by default: a `dump()` left in the code throws an exception in production instead of leaking data. Enable it explicitly, only in development:

```php
use Foundry\Debug;

Debug::enable(Env::bool('APP_DEBUG', false));
```

## Ending a request

`Response::send()` sends the response but does not stop the script. Always follow it with `return` (or `exit`):

```php
use Foundry\Response;

Response::redirect('/clients')->send();

return;
```

---

# Design principles

> The rules every Foundry class follows - explicit errors, one file per tool, pure native PHP, no personal data in error messages - and what is deliberately left out.

Canonical: https://foundry.insightdevhub.ro/docs/design-principles/

## The rules

**Explicit errors.** Any error throws an exception that names the operation, its context and the root cause. No silent `false` or `null` return values for error states.

**One file = one tool.** There are no dependencies between utility files. A little duplicated code across files is preferred over links between them, so any single file can be copied on its own.

**Pure native PHP.** No third-party packages. Composer is only a development tool of the library (tests, static analysis, code style), never a runtime requirement.

**Standard SPL exceptions.** `InvalidArgumentException`, `RuntimeException`, `UnexpectedValueException`, `LogicException` and friends. No custom exception hierarchy to import or learn.

**The `Foundry` namespace.** Names like `Log`, `Str` or `Arr` are common; the namespace removes any risk of collision with your own classes.

**No side effects on require.** Including a file never changes global state. Classes that do (`ErrorHandler`, `Session`) must be activated explicitly.

**Native warnings converted internally.** PHP warnings raised inside a class are caught and become the cause of the exception, whatever error handler the host application uses.

**No personal data in error messages.** Exceptions report metadata (type, length, path), never customer or sensitive data.

**Data over HTML.** UI helpers (`Flash`, `Breadcrumbs`, `FormBuilder`) return arrays and data structures. Markup, CSS classes and escaping stay in your templates, so any template engine or design system works.

## Code conventions

- `declare(strict_types=1)`, `final` classes and strict comparisons everywhere.
- Static analysis at the strictest level (PHPStan max) with no ignored errors and no baseline.
- Every file header has a description, a usage example, `@version` and `@since`.
- Every public method documents its parameters, return value and the exceptions it throws.
- The `@` error suppression operator is never used.

## Deliberately left out

Some things are not part of Foundry on purpose:

- **Custom exception hierarchies and assertion libraries.** Native types, `Validator` and `Cast` cover the same ground.
- **HTML builders and translation engines.** They would tie you to one template engine and one translation store.
- **Polyfills for features already native in PHP 8.3**, such as `str_contains()`, `array_is_list()`, `json_validate()` or `password_hash()`.

---

# PHP versions

> Foundry is written for PHP 8.3+ and can be downgraded automatically to PHP 7.4. Here is how the two targets relate and how they differ.

Canonical: https://foundry.insightdevhub.ro/docs/php-versions/

## Supported versions

| Target | Role |
| --- | --- |
| PHP 8.3+ | The source code. Every class is written, tested and documented for this version. |
| PHP 7.4 | Generated from the same source by an automated downgrade, for older servers. |

The download archive contains the PHP 8.3 sources. This documentation describes the PHP 8.3 API; the PHP 7.4 build exposes the same classes, methods and exceptions.

PHP 5.x is not supported.

## How the PHP 7.4 build is made

The PHP 7.4 files are never edited by hand. They are regenerated from the PHP 8.3 sources:

1. [Rector](https://getrector.com/) rewrites newer syntax (typed class constants, readonly properties, `match`, union types and more) into PHP 7.4 equivalents.
2. Missing PHP 8 functions used by the library, such as `get_debug_type()`, are added as small polyfills.
3. The result is checked with PHP 7.4.33: a syntax check of every file, then a real execution test.

## Differences on PHP 7.4

The behavior is the same, with two differences that come from the PHP engine itself:

- `SQLite` (pdo_sqlite) returns numeric columns as strings (`'2'`) instead of integers. Native driver types arrived in PHP 8.1.
- `gd` image handles are resources instead of `GdImage` objects. This is transparent when you use `Image`.

> **Note:** Named arguments, used in many examples in this documentation (`batchSize: 5000`), are PHP 8 syntax. On PHP 7.4, pass the arguments by position instead.

---

# Form handling

> A complete form workflow with Foundry - reading the request, CSRF protection, validation, saving, flash messages and the redirect.

Canonical: https://foundry.insightdevhub.ro/docs/form-handling/

This guide puts together `Request`, `Csrf`, `Validator`, `RoValidator`, `Session`, `Flash` and `Response` in the classic POST / redirect / GET flow.

## The controller

```php
use Foundry\Csrf;
use Foundry\Flash;
use Foundry\Request;
use Foundry\Response;
use Foundry\RoValidator;
use Foundry\Session;
use Foundry\Validator;

$request = Request::fromGlobals();

if ($request->isPost()) {
    Csrf::check();                                    // invalid token -> exception (HTTP status 419)

    $validator = new Validator($request->all(), [
        'email' => 'required|email|max:255',
        'cnp' => ['required', 'cnp' => RoValidator::cnp(...)],
        'birth_date' => 'required|date:d.m.Y',
    ]);

    if ($validator->fails()) {
        Session::flashInput($request->only('email', 'birth_date'));
        Session::flash('errors', $validator->errors());
        Response::redirect('/clients/new')->send();

        return;
    }

    $db->insert('clients', $validator->validated());
    Flash::success('Client was saved successfully.');
    Response::redirect('/clients')->send();

    return;
}
```

## Step by step

1. `Request::fromGlobals()` wraps the superglobals with typed getters. `$request->int('id')` returns an integer or throws: a missing value, an array (`?id[]=1`) or `'12abc'` never slips through.
2. `Csrf::check()` verifies the session-bound token for POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE requests and throws when it is missing or wrong.
3. `Validator` applies rules per field. Invalid data does **not** throw: each field gets one error, with a stable code (`codes()`) and a message (`errors()`).
4. Custom rules are closures. `RoValidator` methods return booleans, so they plug in directly as `'cnp' => RoValidator::cnp(...)`.
5. On failure, the input and the errors are flashed to the session and the user is redirected back to the form.
6. On success, `validated()` returns only the validated fields, ready for `insert()`. A flash message confirms the result after the redirect.

> **Warning:** `Response::send()` does not stop the script. The `return` after each redirect is required.

## The template

The UI helpers return data, not HTML, so the markup stays yours. Use `e()` (or `View::escape()`) for every value you print:

```php
<?php use function Foundry\e; ?>
<?php foreach (Flash::pull() as $message): ?>
    <div class="alert alert-<?= e($message['type']) ?>"><?= e($message['message']) ?></div>
<?php endforeach ?>

<form method="post" action="/clients/new">
    <?= Csrf::field() ?>

    <label for="email">Email</label>
    <input id="email" name="email" value="<?= e(Session::old('email')) ?>">
    <?php if (isset(Session::flashed('errors', [])['email'])): ?>
        <p class="error"><?= e(Session::flashed('errors')['email']) ?></p>
    <?php endif ?>

    <button type="submit">Save</button>
</form>
```

## Public forms

For forms anyone can submit (contact, registration, password reset), add `BotDetection` (a honeypot field plus a signed minimum fill time) and `RateLimiter` (for example 5 attempts per minute per IP address).

---

# Large imports and exports

> Import and export millions of CSV and Excel rows with constant memory - schema validation, batches, resumable cursors and streaming writers.

Canonical: https://foundry.insightdevhub.ro/docs/imports-exports/

`Csv` and `Xlsx` process millions of rows with constant memory. Everything is streamed inside your own loop: nothing is loaded into memory as a whole, and you decide when to write to the database and when to stop.

| Benchmark: 1,000,000 rows | Time | Peak memory |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CSV import | 8.1 s | 71 MB |
| `.xlsx` import | 13.5 s | 69 MB |

## Reading

```php
use Foundry\Csv;

foreach (Csv::read('customers.csv') as $row => $values) {
    // $values['name'], $values['email'] ...
}
```

`Csv::read()` takes the header from the first row, detects the delimiter, strips the BOM and converts legacy Windows-1250 files to UTF-8. Rows with the wrong number of fields are reported as errors instead of being silently shifted. `Xlsx::read()` works the same way for Excel files.

## Importing with a schema

`Csv::import()` and `Xlsx::import()` validate and normalize rows against a schema and deliver them in batches:

```php
$schema = [
    'cnp' => ['required' => true, 'pattern' => '/^\d{13}$/', 'unique' => true],
    'name' => ['required' => true, 'max' => 100],
    'birth_date' => ['type' => 'date', 'format' => 'd.m.Y'],
    'amount' => ['type' => 'decimal', 'scale' => 2, 'decimal' => ','],
    'type' => ['in' => ['PF', 'PJ']],
];
```

Each batch contains the valid rows (`rows`), the errors found (`errors`, with file, row, column and a stable code), per-file statistics (`files`), a resume `cursor`, and a `done` flag.

```php
$start = microtime(true);

foreach (Csv::import($files, $schema, batchSize: 5000, cursor: $cursor) as $batch) {
    $db->insertMany('customers', array_column($batch['rows'], 'data'));
    $errors = [...$errors, ...$batch['errors']];        // keep them for the import report
    $cursor = $batch['cursor'];                          // save it to resume later

    if ($batch['done'] || microtime(true) - $start > 20) {
        break;                                           // the next request resumes from $cursor
    }
}
```

## Resumable imports

The cursor is a JSON-serializable array. Store it (in the session, the database or a file) and pass it back on the next request: the import continues where it stopped, without re-reading processed files. This keeps each web request under its time limit, however large the upload.

For large `.xlsx` uploads, `Xlsx::stage()` prepares the workbook once so that later requests read from the staged work file.

Batch transactions and time limits stay in your code: the library never decides when to commit or when to stop.

## Writing

Writers receive rows one by one and create the final file atomically when you call `close()`:

```php
$out = Csv::writer('report.csv');                    // header from the first row's keys
foreach ($db->cursor('SELECT * FROM customers') as $row) {
    $out->add($row);
}
$out->close();
```

CSV files are written as UTF-8 with BOM, `;` as delimiter and CRLF line endings, so Excel opens them correctly. Values starting with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` are prefixed to prevent formula execution (CSV injection). `Xlsx::writer()` splits very large exports into several files when a sheet would exceed the Excel row limit.

---

# Databases

> MySQL, Oracle and SQLite share one API - fetch helpers, array-based insert/update/delete, streaming cursors, transactions and safe pagination.

Canonical: https://foundry.insightdevhub.ro/docs/databases/

`MySQL`, `Oracle` and `SQLite` are thin, strict wrappers with an **identical public API**. Code written against one of them reads the same with the others; only the constructor changes.

## Connecting

```php
use Foundry\Env;
use Foundry\MySQL;
use Foundry\SQLite;

$db = new MySQL(
    host: Env::string('DB_HOST'),
    database: Env::string('DB_DATABASE'),
    username: Env::string('DB_USERNAME'),
    password: Env::string('DB_PASSWORD'),
);

$local = new SQLite(__DIR__.'/data/app.db');          // a missing file is an error, never silently created
```

Connections open lazily on the first query. Credentials have no defaults, and the password parameter is marked `#[SensitiveParameter]`, so it never appears in stack traces.

## The shared API

| Method | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `fetchAll()` | All rows as associative arrays. |
| `fetchOne()` | One row or `null`; fails if the query returns more than one row. |
| `fetchOneOrFail()` | One row, or an exception when there is none. |
| `fetchValue()` | The first column of a single row, for example `SELECT COUNT(*)`. |
| `fetchColumn()` | One column as a list. |
| `fetchPairs()` | Key / value pairs; duplicate keys are rejected instead of overwritten. |
| `execute()` | Any statement; returns the number of affected rows. |
| `insert()`, `insertGetId()` | Insert one row from an array. |
| `insertMany()` | Insert many rows, chunked, inside a single transaction. |
| `update()`, `delete()` | Array-based conditions; unconditional updates and deletes are rejected. |
| `cursor()` | A generator that streams rows one at a time. |
| `transaction()` | Runs a closure in a transaction; commits on success, rolls back on any exception. |
| `paginate()` | One page of results plus the total count. |
| `whereIn()` | Builds a safe `IN (...)` fragment with its parameters. |

## Queries and parameters

```php
$users = $db->fetchAll('SELECT * FROM users WHERE active = ?', [1]);
$user = $db->fetchOneOrFail('SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = :id', ['id' => $id]);

$id = $db->insertGetId('users', ['name' => 'Ion', 'email' => 'ion@example.com']);
$db->update('users', ['active' => 0], ['id' => $id]);

$db->transaction(function (MySQL $db) use ($order): void {
    $db->insert('orders', $order);
    $db->execute('UPDATE stock SET qty = qty - 1 WHERE product_id = ?', [$order['product_id']]);
});
```

Parameters are positional (`?`) or named (`:id`), never mixed. Table and column names passed to `insert()`, `update()` and `delete()` are validated and quoted. With MySQL, native prepared statements are used (no emulation), the connection is `utf8mb4`, and several statements in one call are rejected.

## Engine specifics

- **MySQL**: `INT` and `FLOAT` columns come back as `int` / `float`; `DECIMAL` stays a string to keep its precision.
- **Oracle** (oci8): ORA errors become exceptions; targets Oracle 11.2.0.4+ (`ROWNUM` pagination), with `nextVal()` for sequences.
- **SQLite**: the `foreign_keys` pragma is enabled; missing database files are never created implicitly.

## Pagination from the URL

`Paginator` reads the page, sort and search parameters from the query string and accepts only whitelisted columns, so they are safe to put into SQL. See the `Paginator` reference for the full API.

---

# ErrorHandler

> Explicitly registered: converts warnings to ErrorException, logs deprecations, handles uncaught exceptions and fatal errors with logging and a generic 500 response (detailed traces in debug mode only).

Canonical: https://foundry.insightdevhub.ro/docs/error-handler/  
Namespace: `Foundry\ErrorHandler` · File: `ErrorHandler.php` · Version 1.1 · PHP 8.3+

Application safety net, explicitly activated:

- PHP warnings and notices are converted into ErrorException (no longer pass silently)
- deprecations are only forwarded to the logger (a PHP update won't break pages)
- uncaught exceptions are forwarded to the logger and return a 500 response: generic in production, detailed only in debug mode
- fatal errors (out of memory, execution time exceeded, syntax error in an include) are caught at shutdown and handled identically, with reserved memory freed beforehand.

## Rules

- including this file changes nothing; register() enables handling, unregister() restores previous handlers
- error_reporting() and the @ operator are respected
- default response is plain text or JSON (based on Accept header), without HTML or data leaks in production; custom response rendering can be provided via $renderer
- in CLI, details are sent to STDERR with exit code 255
- in production, display_errors must be Off (server configuration is not modified).

## Usage

```php
require_once 'ErrorHandler.php';
use Foundry\ErrorHandler;

ErrorHandler::register(
    debug: $config['debug'],
    logger: fn (Throwable $e) => $log->error('Uncaught exception', ['exception' => $e]),
    renderer: fn (Throwable $e, bool $debug) => print $view->render('errors/500', ['debug' => $debug]),
);

// inside a front controller with its own try/catch:
catch (Throwable $e) { ErrorHandler::handleException($e); }
```

## Installation

```php
require_once __DIR__.'/lib/Utilities/ErrorHandler.php';

use Foundry\ErrorHandler;
```

## Methods

### register()

```php
public static function register(bool $debug = false, ?Closure $logger = null, ?Closure $renderer = null): void
```

Registers error and exception handlers.

Parameters:
- `$debug` (`bool`, default `false`): true = detailed output in response (development only).
- `$logger` (`(Closure(Throwable): void)|null`, default `null`): Receives uncaught exceptions, fatal errors, and deprecations.
- `$renderer` (`(Closure(Throwable, bool): void)|null`, default `null`): Renders the error response (500 status code is already set).

Throws:
- `LogicException`: If the handler is already registered.

### unregister()

```php
public static function unregister(): void
```

Unregisters the handlers and restores previous error and exception handlers.

Throws:
- `LogicException`: If the handler is not registered.

### isRegistered()

```php
public static function isRegistered(): bool
```

Returns `bool`.

### handleError()

```php
public static function handleError(int $severity, string $message, string $file = '', int $line = 0): bool
```

Warning / notice -> ErrorException; deprecation -> logger.

Parameters:
- `$severity` (`int`, required)
- `$message` (`string`, required)
- `$file` (`string`, default `''`)
- `$line` (`int`, default `0`)

Returns `bool`.

Throws:
- `ErrorException`

### handleException()

```php
public static function handleException(Throwable $exception): void
```

Uncaught exception: logs the error, then renders the error response. Can also be called from application try/catch.

Parameters:
- `$exception` (`Throwable`, required)

### handleShutdown()

```php
public static function handleShutdown(): void
```

Executed on shutdown: fatal error (if any) is handled like an uncaught exception.


---

# Json

> Strict encode/decode, atomic file I/O; preserves large integers, strips BOM safely.

Canonical: https://foundry.insightdevhub.ro/docs/json/  
Namespace: `Foundry\Json` · File: `Json.php` · Version 1.1 · PHP 8.3+

Wrappers for json_encode() / json_decode(). Any error throws an exception; null or false is never returned. Error messages never contain the JSON payload itself (which may contain sensitive personal data).

## Usage

```php
require_once 'Json.php';
use Foundry\Json;

$data = Json::decodeArray($body);               // array or exception
$json = Json::encode(['oras' => 'Iasi']);       // {"oras":"Iasi"}
$config = Json::readArray(__DIR__.'/config.json');
Json::writeFile(__DIR__.'/out.json', $data);             // atomic: temp file + rename
```

## Installation

```php
require_once __DIR__.'/lib/Utilities/Json.php';

use Foundry\Json;
```

## Constants

| Constant | Type | Value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ENCODE_FLAGS` | `int` | `JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE \| JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES \| JSON_PRESERVE_ZERO_FRACTION` | Flags for encode(): readable UTF-8, unescaped slashes, 1.0 preserved as 1.0. |
| `DEPTH` | `int` | `512` | Default maximum depth. |

## Methods

### decode()

```php
public static function decode(string $json, bool $associative = true, int $depth = self::DEPTH): mixed
```

Decodes a JSON string. By default, objects are converted to associative arrays.

Parameters:
- `$json` (`string`, required): The JSON string.
- `$associative` (`bool`, default `true`): true: objects as associative arrays; false: objects as stdClass.
- `$depth` (`int`, default `self::DEPTH`): Maximum depth.

Returns `mixed`: The decoded value (array, scalar, or null for the "null" literal).

Throws:
- `JsonException`: If the JSON is invalid or empty.
- `InvalidArgumentException`: If $depth < 1.

### decodeArray()

```php
public static function decodeArray(string $json, int $depth = self::DEPTH): array
```

Decodes a JSON string that must represent an object or array.

Parameters:
- `$json` (`string`, required): The JSON string.
- `$depth` (`int`, default `self::DEPTH`): Maximum depth.

Returns `array<mixed>`: The decoded array.

Throws:
- `JsonException`: If the JSON is invalid.
- `InvalidArgumentException`: If $depth < 1.
- `UnexpectedValueException`: If the JSON is valid but not an object/array (e.g., "42").

### encode()

```php
public static function encode(mixed $value, bool $pretty = false, int $flags = 0): string
```

Encodes a value as JSON.

Parameters:
- `$value` (`mixed`, required): The value to encode.
- `$pretty` (`bool`, default `false`): true for formatted, indented JSON.
- `$flags` (`int`, default `0`): Additional JSON_* flags combined with ENCODE_FLAGS. JSON_PARTIAL_OUTPUT_ON_ERROR is ignored as it would suppress errors.

Returns `string`: The JSON string.

Throws:
- `JsonException`: On invalid UTF-8, INF/NAN, recursion, or maximum depth exceeded.

### isValid()

```php
public static function isValid(string $json): bool
```

Checks whether a string is valid JSON without throwing an exception.

Parameters:
- `$json` (`string`, required): The string to validate.

Returns `bool`: true if valid.

### readFile()

```php
public static function readFile(string $path): mixed
```

Reads and decodes a JSON file. The UTF-8 BOM is stripped if present.

Parameters:
- `$path` (`string`, required): The file path.

Returns `mixed`: The decoded value.

Throws:
- `RuntimeException`: If the file does not exist or cannot be read.
- `JsonException`: If the file does not contain valid JSON.

### readArray()

```php
public static function readArray(string $path): array
```

Reads a JSON file that must contain an object or array.

Parameters:
- `$path` (`string`, required): The file path.

Returns `array<mixed>`: The decoded array.

Throws:
- `RuntimeException`: If the file does not exist or cannot be read.
- `JsonException`: If the file does not contain valid JSON.
- `UnexpectedValueException`: If the JSON is not an object or array.

### writeFile()

```php
public static function writeFile(string $path, mixed $value, bool $pretty = true): void
```

Encodes a value and writes it to a file atomically: the content goes to a temporary file in the same directory, which then replaces the target with rename(). Readers see either the old or the new content, never an empty or truncated file, and a crash mid-write leaves the old file intact.

Parameters:
- `$path` (`string`, required): The file path; the directory must already exist.
- `$value` (`mixed`, required): The value to encode.
- `$pretty` (`bool`, default `true`): true for formatted, indented JSON (default for files).

Throws:
- `JsonException`: If the value cannot be encoded.
- `RuntimeException`: If the file cannot be written.

# File

> Streaming reads, atomic writes, stream-based copying, safe directory creation (concurrency-safe), MIME detection from file bytes.

Canonical: https://foundry.insightdevhub.ro/docs/file/  
Namespace: `Foundry\File` · File: `File.php` · Version 1.1 · PHP 8.3+ · Extensions: fileinfo

File and directory operations. Native PHP functions return false and emit warnings; here any error throws a RuntimeException with a clear message (operation, path, cause).

## Usage

```php
require_once 'File.php';
use Foundry\File;

File::ensureDir(__DIR__.'/storage/exports');
File::write(__DIR__.'/storage/exports/report.txt', $content);   // atomic write
foreach (File::lines($path) as $number => $line) { ... }          // large files, line by line
$csvFiles = File::files(__DIR__.'/import', extension: 'csv');
File::copyStream($httpBody, __DIR__.'/storage/download.pdf');     // stream -> file, atomic
File::assertWritable(__DIR__.'/storage/logs');                    // exception with exact reason
```

## Installation

```php
require_once __DIR__.'/lib/Utilities/File.php';

use Foundry\File;
```

## Methods

### read()

```php
public static function read(string $path): string
```

Reads the entire contents of a file.

Parameters:
- `$path` (`string`, required): The file path.

Returns `string`: The contents.

Throws:
- `RuntimeException`: If the file does not exist or cannot be read.

### lines()

```php
public static function lines(string $path): Generator
```

Reads a file line by line without loading it completely into memory. Line terminators ("\n", "\r\n") are stripped.

Parameters:
- `$path` (`string`, required): The file path.

Returns `Generator<int, string>`: The key is the 1-based line number.

Throws:
- `RuntimeException`: If the file does not exist or cannot be opened.

### write()

```php
public static function write(string $path, string $content): void
```

Writes content to a file atomically: writes to a temporary file in the same directory, then renames it. A reader sees either the old file or the complete new one. Permissions of an existing file are preserved.

Parameters:
- `$path` (`string`, required): The file path; the directory must exist.
- `$content` (`string`, required): The content to write.

Throws:
- `RuntimeException`: If the directory does not exist or writing fails.

### copyStream()

```php
public static function copyStream($source, string $path): int
```

Copies a stream (e.g. an HTTP response body, php://input, an open file) into a file atomically without buffering the entire stream in memory. The stream is read to EOF.

Parameters:
- `$source` (`resource`, required): The source stream, opened for reading.
- `$path` (`string`, required): The destination file; the directory must exist.

Returns `int`: The number of bytes written.

Throws:
- `InvalidArgumentException`: If $source is not a stream resource.
- `RuntimeException`: If reading or writing fails, or stops before EOF.

### writeAll()

```php
public static function writeAll($handle, string $data): void
```

Writes all data to an open stream. fwrite() may write fewer bytes than provided (sockets, pipes, disk full) without error; this method continues until completion or throws an exception.

Parameters:
- `$handle` (`resource`, required): Stream resource open for writing.
- `$data` (`string`, required): The data to write.

Throws:
- `InvalidArgumentException`: If $handle is not a stream resource.
- `RuntimeException`: If writing fails or makes no progress.

### append()

```php
public static function append(string $path, string $content): void
```

Appends content to the end of a file (creates it if it does not exist), using an exclusive lock.

Parameters:
- `$path` (`string`, required): The file path; the directory must exist.
- `$content` (`string`, required): The content to append.

Throws:
- `RuntimeException`: If the directory does not exist or writing fails.

### delete()

```php
public static function delete(string $path): void
```

Deletes a file. A missing file is considered an error.

Parameters:
- `$path` (`string`, required): The file path.

Throws:
- `RuntimeException`: If the file does not exist or cannot be deleted.

### deleteIfExists()

```php
public static function deleteIfExists(string $path): bool
```

Deletes a file if it exists.

Parameters:
- `$path` (`string`, required): The file path.

Returns `bool`: true if the file was deleted, false if it did not exist.

Throws:
- `RuntimeException`: If the file exists but cannot be deleted.

### copy()

```php
public static function copy(string $from, string $to): void
```

Copies a file. An existing destination file is overwritten.

Parameters:
- `$from` (`string`, required): The source file.
- `$to` (`string`, required): The destination file; the directory must exist.

Throws:
- `RuntimeException`: If the source file does not exist or copying fails.

### move()

```php
public static function move(string $from, string $to): void
```

Moves or renames a file. An existing destination file is overwritten. Across different partitions/drives PHP automatically performs a copy + delete; in that case the move is no longer atomic.

Parameters:
- `$from` (`string`, required): The source file.
- `$to` (`string`, required): The destination file; the directory must exist.

Throws:
- `RuntimeException`: If the source does not exist or moving fails.

### ensureDir()

```php
public static function ensureDir(string $dir, int $mode = 0775): void
```

Ensures that a directory exists (creates it recursively if missing). Safe under concurrent requests: if another process created it concurrently, no error is thrown.

Parameters:
- `$dir` (`string`, required): The directory path.
- `$mode` (`int`, default `509`): Permissions (Linux), affected by umask.

Throws:
- `RuntimeException`: If a file with the same name exists or creation fails.

### deleteDir()


Recursively deletes a directory and all of its contents. Symlinks are deleted as links; target contents are untouched.

Parameters:
- `$dir` (`string`, required): The directory path.

Throws:
- `RuntimeException`: If the directory does not exist, is a filesystem root, or deletion fails.

### files()


Lists files in a directory (excluding subdirectories by default), sorted alphabetically.

Parameters:
- `$dir` (`string`, required): The directory path.

- `$extension` (`string|null`, default `null`): Filter by extension without leading dot (e.g. 'csv'); case-insensitive.

Returns `list<string>`: Absolute paths of the files.

Throws:

### size()

File size in bytes.

# Regex

> Strict preg_* wrapper throwing exceptions on invalid patterns or execution failures.

Canonical: https://foundry.insightdevhub.ro/docs/regex/  
Namespace: `Foundry\Regex` · File: `Regex.php` · Version 1.1 · PHP 8.3+

Wrappers over preg_* functions. Natively, an invalid pattern emits only a warning and returns false/null, while runtime execution errors (backtracking limit, invalid UTF-8) go completely unnoticed. Here:

- invalid pattern    -> InvalidArgumentException (programming error)
- execution error    -> RuntimeException (the message does not contain the analyzed text)

Unmatched capture groups are returned as null (not empty strings).

## Usage

```php
require_once 'Regex.php';
use Foundry\Regex;

if (Regex::test('/^RO\d{2}[A-Z]{4}/', $iban)) { ... }
$m = Regex::match('/^(?<judet>[A-Z]{1,2}) ?(?<numar>\d{2,3})/', 'B 123 ABC');  // $m['judet'] === 'B'
$slug = Regex::replace('/[^a-z0-9]+/', '-', $text);
$words = Regex::split('/\s+/', $text, removeEmpty: true);
```

## Installation

```php
require_once __DIR__.'/lib/Utilities/Regex.php';

use Foundry\Regex;
```

## Methods

### test()

```php
public static function test(string $pattern, string $subject): bool
```

Checks whether the pattern matches against the string.

Parameters:
- `$pattern` (`string`, required): The regular expression, including delimiters (e.g. '/^\d+$/').
- `$subject` (`string`, required): The input string.

Returns `bool`: True if a match is found.

Throws:
- `InvalidArgumentException`: If the pattern is invalid.
- `RuntimeException`: On execution error.

### match()

```php
public static function match(string $pattern, string $subject): ?array
```

First match: [0 => full matched text, 1 => group 1, 'name' => named group, ...].

Parameters:
- `$pattern` (`string`, required): The regular expression.
- `$subject` (`string`, required): The input string.

Returns `array<int|string, string|null>|null`: The matches or null if no match was found.

Throws:
- `InvalidArgumentException`: If the pattern is invalid.
- `RuntimeException`: On execution error.

### matchAll()

```php
public static function matchAll(string $pattern, string $subject): array
```

All matches, each with its captured groups (PREG_SET_ORDER).

Parameters:
- `$pattern` (`string`, required): The regular expression.
- `$subject` (`string`, required): The input string.

Returns `list<array<int|string, string|null>>`: List of matches (empty if none found).

Throws:
- `InvalidArgumentException`: If the pattern is invalid.
- `RuntimeException`: On execution error.

### replace()

```php
public static function replace(string $pattern, string $replacement, string $subject, int $limit = -1): string
```

Replaces matches with replacement text ($1, ${name} are allowed in replacement).

Parameters:
- `$pattern` (`string`, required): The regular expression.
- `$replacement` (`string`, required): The replacement text.
- `$subject` (`string`, required): The input string.
- `$limit` (`int`, default `-1`): The maximum number of replacements; -1 = unlimited.

Returns `string`: The resulting string.

Throws:
- `InvalidArgumentException`: If the pattern is invalid.
- `RuntimeException`: On execution error.

### replaceCallback()

```php
public static function replaceCallback(string $pattern, Closure $callback, string $subject, int $limit = -1): string
```

Replaces matches with the result of a callback function.

Parameters:
- `$pattern` (`string`, required): The regular expression.
- `$callback` (`Closure`, required)
- `$subject` (`string`, required): The input string.
- `$limit` (`int`, default `-1`): The maximum number of replacements; -1 = unlimited.

Returns `string`: The resulting string.

Throws:
- `InvalidArgumentException`: If the pattern is invalid.
- `RuntimeException`: On execution error.

### split()

```php
public static function split(string $pattern, string $subject, int $limit = -1, bool $removeEmpty = false): array
```

Splits a string by a pattern.

Parameters:
- `$pattern` (`string`, required): The regular expression used as a separator.
- `$subject` (`string`, required): The string to split.
- `$limit` (`int`, default `-1`): The maximum number of substrings; -1 = unlimited.
- `$removeEmpty` (`bool`, default `false`): True to remove empty substrings.

Returns `list<string>`: The substrings.

Throws:
- `InvalidArgumentException`: If the pattern is invalid.
- `RuntimeException`: On execution error.

### filter()

```php
public static function filter(string $pattern, array $items, bool $invert = false): array
```

Keeps only elements that match the pattern (keys are preserved).

Parameters:
- `$pattern` (`string`, required): The regular expression.
- `$items` (`array<array-key, string>`, required): The elements to filter.
- `$invert` (`bool`, default `false`): True to keep elements that do NOT match.

Returns `array<array-key, string>`: The kept elements.

Throws:
- `InvalidArgumentException`: If the pattern is invalid.
- `RuntimeException`: On execution error.

# Cast

> Strict type conversions toInt/toFloat/toBool/toString (rejects '12abc', '1,5', '').

Canonical: https://foundry.insightdevhub.ro/docs/cast/  
Namespace: `Foundry\Cast` · File: `Cast.php` · Version 1.1 · PHP 8.3+

Strict type casting for values originating externally (forms, CSV, APIs, databases). Natively, (int) 'abc' = 0, intval('12abc') = 12, (float) '1.234,50' = 1.234, all without errors. Here, any value that does not precisely represent the requested type throws an exception.

## Rules

- leading and trailing whitespace is ignored for strings
- decimals use a dot separator ("1.5"); for Romanian formatting ("1.234,50") see Number
- OrNull variants return null for null and empty (or whitespace-only) strings
- error messages include the value type, never the raw value.

## Usage

```php
require_once 'Cast.php';
use Foundry\Cast;

$id = Cast::toInt($_GET['id'] ?? null);          // "12" -> 12; "12abc", "", null -> exception
$amount = Cast::toFloat($row['suma']);           // "150.5" -> 150.5
$active = Cast::toBool($row['activ']);           // "da", "1", "true", "on" -> true
$page = Cast::toIntOrNull($_GET['page'] ?? null) ?? 1;
```

## Installation

```php
require_once __DIR__.'/lib/Utilities/Cast.php';

use Foundry\Cast;
```

## Methods

### toInt()

```php
public static function toInt(mixed $value): int
```

Casts to int: int, float without fractional part (3.0), or numeric string ("12", "-5", "+5").

Parameters:
- `$value` (`mixed`, required)

Returns `int`.

Throws:
- `InvalidArgumentException`: If the value does not represent an exact integer.

### toFloat()

```php
public static function toFloat(mixed $value): float
```

Casts to float: int, finite float, or numeric string with a dot separator ("1.5", "1e3").

Parameters:
- `$value` (`mixed`, required)

Returns `float`.

Throws:
- `InvalidArgumentException`: If the value is not a valid number (or is NAN/INF).

### toBool()

```php
public static function toBool(mixed $value): bool
```

Casts to bool: bool, int 0/1, or one of the case-insensitive strings: true/false, 1/0, yes/no, on/off, da/nu.

Parameters:
- `$value` (`mixed`, required)

Returns `bool`.

Throws:
- `InvalidArgumentException`: For any other value (including empty string and null).

### toString()

```php
public static function toString(mixed $value): string
```

Casts to string: string, int, finite float, or Stringable object. bool, null, array, and other objects are rejected (their conversion is ambiguous).

Parameters:
- `$value` (`mixed`, required)

Returns `string`.

Throws:
- `InvalidArgumentException`: If the value cannot be unambiguously converted.

### toIntOrNull()

```php
public static function toIntOrNull(mixed $value): ?int
```

Same as toInt(), but null and empty string return null.

Parameters:
- `$value` (`mixed`, required)

Returns `?int`.

Throws:
- `InvalidArgumentException`: If the value is non-empty and does not represent an integer.

### toFloatOrNull()

```php
public static function toFloatOrNull(mixed $value): ?float
```

Same as toFloat(), but null and empty string return null.

Parameters:
- `$value` (`mixed`, required)

Returns `?float`.

Throws:
- `InvalidArgumentException`: If the value is non-empty and is not a number.

### toBoolOrNull()

```php
public static function toBoolOrNull(mixed $value): ?bool
```

Same as toBool(), but null and empty string return null.

Parameters:
- `$value` (`mixed`, required)

Returns `?bool`.

Throws:
- `InvalidArgumentException`: If the value is non-empty and is not a recognized boolean representation.

### toStringOrNull()

```php
public static function toStringOrNull(mixed $value): ?string
```

Same as toString(), but null and empty (or whitespace-only) string return null.

Parameters:
- `$value` (`mixed`, required)

Returns `?string`.

Throws:
- `InvalidArgumentException`: If the value is non-empty and cannot be converted.

# Encoding

> Windows-1250 <-> UTF-8 conversion, Romanian cedilla <-> comma normalization, UTF-8 validity verification, BOM detection.

Canonical: https://foundry.insightdevhub.ro/docs/encoding/  
Namespace: `Foundry\Encoding` · File: `Encoding.php` · Version 1.0 · PHP 8.3+ · Extensions: mbstring, iconv

Character encoding conversions, with a focus on Romanian text from legacy systems (Excel, CSV exported from Windows, Latin2 databases).

Natively, iconv() returns false with a notice on illegal characters, while mb_convert_encoding() silently replaces invalid characters with "?". In addition, mbstring does not recognize Windows-1250, which is why conversions are performed using iconv.

## About Romanian diacritics

- the correct form uses a comma: s, t with comma below (U+0219, U+021B, U+0218, U+021A)
- legacy systems use the cedilla form (U+015F, U+0163, U+015E, U+0162)
- Windows-1250 and ISO-8859-2 contain ONLY the cedilla form; therefore fromUtf8() to these encodings automatically converts comma to cedilla.

An 8-bit encoding cannot be reliably detected (the same bytes are valid across many encodings); therefore detect() is not provided, but ensureUtf8() with an explicitly declared fallback encoding.

## Usage

```php
require_once 'Encoding.php';
use Foundry\Encoding;

$text = Encoding::ensureUtf8(File::read('import.csv'));        // UTF-8 or Windows-1250 -> UTF-8
$text = Encoding::fixRomanianDiacritics($text);                // cedilla -> comma
$legacy = Encoding::fromUtf8($text, 'Windows-1250');           // for a legacy system
```

## Installation

```php
require_once __DIR__.'/lib/Utilities/Encoding.php';

use Foundry\Encoding;
```

## Constants

| Constant | Type | Value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `BOM` | `string` | `"\xEF\xBB\xBF"` | UTF-8 BOM. |

## Methods

### isUtf8()

```php
public static function isUtf8(string $text): bool
```

Checks whether the string is valid UTF-8.

Parameters:
- `$text` (`string`, required)

Returns `bool`.

### assertUtf8()

```php
public static function assertUtf8(string $text): void
```

Throws an exception if the string is not valid UTF-8.

Parameters:
- `$text` (`string`, required)

Throws:
- `UnexpectedValueException`: If the string contains invalid UTF-8 sequences.

### toUtf8()

```php
public static function toUtf8(string $text, string $from): string
```

Converts text from the $from encoding to UTF-8.

Parameters:
- `$text` (`string`, required): The text to convert.
- `$from` (`string`, required): The source encoding (e.g. 'Windows-1250', 'ISO-8859-2', 'UTF-16LE').

Returns `string`.

Throws:
- `InvalidArgumentException`: If the encoding is not supported.
- `UnexpectedValueException`: If the text contains invalid bytes for $from.

### ensureUtf8()

```php
public static function ensureUtf8(string $text, string $fallback = 'Windows-1250'): string
```

Returns the text in UTF-8: unchanged if already valid UTF-8, otherwise converted from $fallback. Suitable for imported files whose encoding is not known in advance.

Parameters:
- `$text` (`string`, required): The text.
- `$fallback` (`string`, default `'Windows-1250'`): The assumed encoding if the text is not UTF-8.

Returns `string`.

Throws:
- `InvalidArgumentException`: If $fallback is not supported.
- `UnexpectedValueException`: If the text is not valid in $fallback either.

### fromUtf8()

```php
public static function fromUtf8(string $text, string $to): string
```

Converts UTF-8 text to another encoding. For Windows-1250 / ISO-8859-2, diacritics with comma are first converted to cedilla.

Parameters:
- `$text` (`string`, required): UTF-8 text.
- `$to` (`string`, required): The target encoding.

Returns `string`.

Throws:
- `InvalidArgumentException`: If the encoding is not supported.
- `UnexpectedValueException`: If the text is not valid UTF-8 or contains characters that do not exist in the target encoding.

### fixRomanianDiacritics()

```php
public static function fixRomanianDiacritics(string $text): string
```

Replaces diacritics with cedilla (legacy form) with the correct form with comma. The text must be UTF-8.

Parameters:
- `$text` (`string`, required)

Returns `string`.

### legacyRomanianDiacritics()

```php
public static function legacyRomanianDiacritics(string $text): string
```

Replaces diacritics with comma with the cedilla form, for systems that do not recognize the correct form. The text must be UTF-8.

Parameters:
- `$text` (`string`, required)

Returns `string`.

### stripBom()

```php
public static function stripBom(string $text): string
```

Removes the UTF-8 BOM from the beginning of the text, if present.

Parameters:
- `$text` (`string`, required)

Returns `string`.

# Upload

> Secure file uploads: MIME detection from file inspection, whitelist-checked extension, cryptographically random names.

Canonical: https://foundry.insightdevhub.ro/docs/upload/  
Namespace: `Foundry\Upload` · File: `Upload.php` · Version 1.0 · PHP 8.3+ · Extensions: mbstring, fileinfo

Validation and storage of files uploaded through forms ($_FILES).

## Security rules

- file MIME type is detected from content (finfo), not from $_FILES['type'] (sent by client)
- the saved file extension comes from the allowed types list, NOT from the client-provided name (a "invoice.php.jpg" or PHP script disguised as a PDF cannot reach disk with an executable extension)
- the saved file name is randomly generated (or explicitly provided and validated); nothing is overwritten
- only files genuinely uploaded via HTTP POST are accepted (is_uploaded_file).

## Exceptions

- InvalidArgumentException: user file is rejected (missing, too large, disallowed type); the message can be translated and displayed to the user
- RuntimeException:         server issue (missing temporary directory, write failure)
- LogicException:           programming error (invalid $_FILES structure, invalid configuration).

## Usage

```php
require_once 'Upload.php';
use Foundry\Upload;

$stored = Upload::store($_FILES['document'], __DIR__.'/storage/uploads', [
    'application/pdf' => 'pdf',
    'image/jpeg' => 'jpg',
    'image/png' => 'png',
], maxSize: 5 * 1024 * 1024);

// $stored['path'], $stored['name'], $stored['originalName'], $stored['size'], $stored['mimeType']

foreach (Upload::files($_FILES['documents']) as $file) { ... }   // <input type="file" multiple>
```

## Installation

```php
require_once __DIR__.'/lib/Utilities/Upload.php';

use Foundry\Upload;
```

## Methods

### store()

```php
public static function store(array $file, string $directory, array $allowed, int $maxSize, ?string $name = null): array
```

Validates the uploaded file and moves it to $directory.

Parameters:
- `$file` (`array<mixed>`, required): An element from $_FILES (e.g. $_FILES['document']).
- `$directory` (`string`, required): Destination directory; must exist and be writable.
- `$allowed` (`array<string, string>`, required): Allowed types: MIME type => saved file extension.
- `$maxSize` (`int`, required): Maximum allowed size in bytes.
- `$name` (`string|null`, default `null`): Saved file name without extension; null = randomly generated.

Returns `array{path: string, name: string, originalName: string, size: int, mimeType: string, extension: string}`.

Throws:
- `InvalidArgumentException`: If the user's file is rejected.
- `RuntimeException`: On server errors or if the target file already exists.
- `LogicException`: On invalid parameters.

### validate()

```php
public static function validate(array $file, array $allowed, int $maxSize): array
```

Validates the uploaded file without moving it: error code, size, actual MIME type. Does not check is_uploaded_file(); use store() to save files.

Parameters:
- `$file` (`array<mixed>`, required): An element from $_FILES.
- `$allowed` (`array<string, string>`, required): Allowed types: MIME type => extension.
- `$maxSize` (`int`, required): Maximum allowed size in bytes.

Returns `array{tmpName: string, originalName: string, size: int, mimeType: string, extension: string}`.

Throws:
- `InvalidArgumentException`: If the user's file is rejected.
- `RuntimeException`: On server errors.
- `LogicException`: On invalid parameters.

### files()

```php
public static function files(array $field): array
```

Converts a multi-file upload field (<input type="file" name="docs[]" multiple>) into a list of individual files, each in standard single-file format. Elements with UPLOAD_ERR_NO_FILE (unfilled fields) are removed.

Parameters:
- `$field` (`array<mixed>`, required): The $_FILES element (e.g. $_FILES['documents']).

Returns `list<array{name: string, type: string, tmp_name: string, error: int, size: int}>`.

Throws:
- `LogicException`: If the structure does not match a $_FILES field.

### maxServerSize()

```php
public static function maxServerSize(): int
```

Maximum upload size accepted by the server in bytes: minimum of upload_max_filesize and post_max_size (0 = unlimited).

Returns `int`.

# Process

> Safe command execution without shell expansion, exit code validation, stdin support, configurable timeouts.

Canonical: https://foundry.insightdevhub.ro/docs/process/  
Namespace: `Foundry\Process` · File: `Process.php` · Version 1.1 · PHP 8.3+

Executes external commands with verified exit codes, separated stdout/stderr, and timeout enforcement.

Natively, shell_exec() returns null on both error and empty output, exec() ignores exit codes unless explicitly captured, and arguments require manual escaping (posing command injection risks). Here, commands are supplied as an argument list: PHP launches them directly without invoking a shell, so arguments are never shell-interpreted (no escaping required, immune to injection).

Output is directed to temporary files rather than pipes: on Windows, stream_select() fails on pipes, and a saturated pipe deadlocks the process.

Error messages expose only the program name, omitting arguments (which may contain sensitive credentials). run() does include the last 1000 bytes of stderr when the exit code is not 0, to explain the failure; for programs that may print secrets or personal data on stderr, use runUnchecked() and handle the output yourself.

On timeout the process receives SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after 2 seconds if it is still running. Processes it started itself (e.g. through "sh -c") are not stopped and may keep running.

## Usage

```php
require_once 'Process.php';
use Foundry\Process;

$result = Process::run(['git', 'log', '-1', '--format=%H'], cwd: __DIR__);
echo $result['stdout'];

$result = Process::run(['mysqldump', '--result-file='.$file, 'database'], timeout: 600);

$result = Process::runUnchecked(['ping', '-n', '1', 'server']);  // does not throw on non-zero exit
if ($result['exitCode'] !== 0) { ... }
```

## Installation

```php
require_once __DIR__.'/lib/Utilities/Process.php';

use Foundry\Process;
```

## Methods

### run()

```php
public static function run(array $command, ?string $cwd = null, ?array $env = null, ?string $input = null, float $timeout = 60.0): array
```

Executes the command and throws an exception if it terminates with a non-zero exit code.

Parameters:
- `$command` (`list<string>`, required): The program and its arguments, e.g. ['git', 'status'].
- `$cwd` (`string|null`, default `null`): The working directory; null = current working directory.
- `$env` (`array<string, string>|null`, default `null`): Environment variables to merge over the current environment; null = inherit.
- `$input` (`string|null`, default `null`): Text sent to stdin.
- `$timeout` (`float`, default `60.0`): Maximum execution time in seconds.

Returns `array{exitCode: int, stdout: string, stderr: string}`.

Throws:
- `InvalidArgumentException`: On invalid parameters.
- `RuntimeException`: If the process fails to start, times out, or exits with code != 0.

### runUnchecked()

```php
public static function runUnchecked(array $command, ?string $cwd = null, ?array $env = null, ?string $input = null, float $timeout = 60.0): array
```

Same as run(), but does NOT throw an exception for a non-zero exit code. Startup failures and timeouts still throw exceptions.

Parameters:
- `$command` (`list<string>`, required): The program and its arguments.
- `$cwd` (`?string`, default `null`)
- `$env` (`array<string, string>|null`, default `null`)
- `$input` (`?string`, default `null`)
- `$timeout` (`float`, default `60.0`)

Returns `array{exitCode: int, stdout: string, stderr: string}`.

Throws:
- `InvalidArgumentException`: On invalid parameters.
- `RuntimeException`: If the process fails to start or times out.


---

# Zip

> Secure archive creation and extraction (protected against zip slip, symlink attacks, and zip bombs).

Canonical: https://foundry.insightdevhub.ro/docs/zip/  
Namespace: `Foundry\Zip` · File: `Zip.php` · Version 1.1 · PHP 8.3+ · Extensions: zip

Creation, listing, and extraction of ZIP archives wrapping ZipArchive.

Natively, ZipArchive::open() returns true OR an integer error code (which is truthy, so "if ($zip->open(...))" passes even on error), while addFile()/close() return false without details.

On extraction, all entries are validated before writing anything to disk:

- unsafe paths ("../", absolute paths, drive letters) -> exception ("zip slip" protection)
- symlinks (Unix archives) -> exception
- "zip bomb" protection: optional limits on the real extracted size ($maxBytes, counted while decompressing, never taken from the archive headers) and on the number of entries ($maxEntries); an entry that decompresses to more than it declares is always rejected.

## Usage

```php
require_once 'Zip.php';
use Foundry\Zip;

Zip::create(__DIR__.'/export.zip', [
    __DIR__.'/report.pdf',                       // in archive: report.pdf
    'attachments/contract.pdf' => $contractPath, // in archive: attachments/contract.pdf
    'documents' => __DIR__.'/storage/docs',      // directory, added recursively
]);

Zip::createFromStrings(__DIR__.'/data.zip', ['data.csv' => $csv, 'info.txt' => 'Automatically generated']);

$files = Zip::extract($uploadedZip, __DIR__.'/import', maxBytes: 100 * 1024 * 1024);
```

## Installation

```php
require_once __DIR__.'/lib/Utilities/Zip.php';

use Foundry\Zip;
```

## Methods

### create()

```php
public static function create(string $zipPath, array $files, bool $overwrite = false): void
```

Creates an archive from existing files and directories.

Parameters:
- `$zipPath` (`string`, required): Archive path; the directory must exist.
- `$files` (`array<int|string, string>`, required): Integer key: archive entry name = file basename; string key: archive entry name (path). Directories are added recursively.
- `$overwrite` (`bool`, default `false`): true: overwrites an existing archive.

Throws:
- `InvalidArgumentException`: If the file list is empty, a file is missing, or a name is unsafe.
- `RuntimeException`: If the archive already exists or cannot be written.

### createFromStrings()

```php
public static function createFromStrings(string $zipPath, array $entries, bool $overwrite = false): void
```

Creates an archive from in-memory string contents.

Parameters:
- `$zipPath` (`string`, required): Archive path; the directory must exist.
- `$entries` (`array<string, string>`, required): Archive entry name => content.
- `$overwrite` (`bool`, default `false`): true: overwrites an existing archive.

Throws:
- `InvalidArgumentException`: If the entry list is empty or a name is unsafe.
- `RuntimeException`: If the archive already exists or cannot be written.

### list()

```php
public static function list(string $zipPath): array
```

List of entries in the archive.

Parameters:
- `$zipPath` (`string`, required)

Returns `list<array{name: string, size: int, compressedSize: int}>`.

Throws:
- `RuntimeException`: If the archive does not exist or cannot be read.

### extract()

```php
public static function extract(string $zipPath, string $directory, ?int $maxBytes = null, ?int $maxEntries = null): array
```

Extracts the archive into $directory after validating ALL entries.

Sizes declared in the archive are controlled by whoever built it, so they are never trusted: every entry is decompressed through a stream and the bytes actually produced are counted. An entry that produces more data than it declares is rejected as tampered, and extraction stops as soon as the real total passes $maxBytes. Files written by a failed call are removed. Error messages identify entries by position (entry #3), never by name.

Parameters:
- `$zipPath` (`string`, required): Archive path.
- `$directory` (`string`, required): Destination directory; must exist.
- `$maxBytes` (`int|null`, default `null`): Maximum total uncompressed size; null = unlimited (only for trusted archives).
- `$maxEntries` (`int|null`, default `null`): Maximum number of entries (files and directories); null = unlimited.

Returns `list<string>`: Names of extracted entries (files and directories), as stored in the archive.

Throws:
- `UnexpectedValueException`: If the archive contains unsafe paths or symlinks, has entries larger than declared, or exceeds $maxBytes / $maxEntries.
- `RuntimeException`: If the archive cannot be read or extraction fails.


---

# Image

> Image metadata, validation against decompression bombs, aspect-ratio resizing, thumbnail generation; requires gd.

Canonical: https://foundry.insightdevhub.ro/docs/image/  
Namespace: `Foundry\Image` · File: `Image.php` · Version 1.2 · PHP 8.3+ · Extensions: gd

Image information, validation, and resizing (JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP) using the gd extension.

Natively, getimagesize() and imagecreatefrom*() return false with a warning, and a small image on disk can declare huge dimensions and exhaust gigabytes of memory upon decoding ("decompression bomb"); validate() verifies pixel counts before decoding, and resize() / thumbnail() also check that the decoded image fits in the remaining memory_limit (~5 bytes per pixel), throwing an exception instead of PHP's uncatchable "Allowed memory size exhausted" fatal error.

resize() and thumbnail() re-encode images, thereby stripping EXIF metadata (GPS, camera model). For animated GIFs, only the first frame is retained.

## Usage

```php
require_once 'Image.php';
use Foundry\Image;

$info = Image::validate($path);                       // ['width' => 1920, 'height' => 1080, 'mimeType' => 'image/jpeg']
Image::resize($path, $dir.'/large.jpg', 1600, 1600);  // fits in 1600x1600, no upscaling
Image::thumbnail($path, $dir.'/thumb.webp', 200, 200);// exact 200x200, center-cropped
```

## Installation

```php
require_once __DIR__.'/lib/Utilities/Image.php';

use Foundry\Image;
```

## Constants

| Constant | Type | Value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `DEFAULT_TYPES` | `list<string>` | `['image/jpeg', 'image/png', 'image/gif', 'image/webp']` | Default image types accepted by validate(). |
| `DEFAULT_MAX_PIXELS` | `int` | `40_000_000` | Default maximum pixel count (40 MP; typical phone photos are 12-50 MP). |

## Methods

### info()

```php
public static function info(string $path): array
```

Image dimensions and type read from headers (without decoding image data).

Parameters:
- `$path` (`string`, required)

Returns `array{width: int, height: int, mimeType: string}`.

Throws:
- `RuntimeException`: If the file does not exist.
- `UnexpectedValueException`: If the file is not a recognized image.

### validate()

```php
public static function validate(
    string $path,
    array $allowedTypes = self::DEFAULT_TYPES,
    int $maxPixels = self::DEFAULT_MAX_PIXELS,
    ?int $maxWidth = null,
    ?int $maxHeight = null,
): array
```

Verifies that the file is an allowed image type within reasonable dimensions.

Parameters:
- `$path` (`string`, required): The image file path.
- `$allowedTypes` (`list<string>`, default `self::DEFAULT_TYPES`): Allowed MIME types.
- `$maxPixels` (`int`, default `self::DEFAULT_MAX_PIXELS`): Maximum pixel count (width x height).
- `$maxWidth` (`int|null`, default `null`): Maximum width; null = no limit.
- `$maxHeight` (`int|null`, default `null`): Maximum height; null = no limit.

Returns `array{width: int, height: int, mimeType: string}`.

Throws:
- `RuntimeException`: If the file does not exist.
- `UnexpectedValueException`: If the image is invalid or exceeds dimension limits.

### resize()

```php
public static function resize(string $source, string $target, int $maxWidth, int $maxHeight, int $quality = 85): array
```

Resizes an image to fit within $maxWidth x $maxHeight while preserving aspect ratio. Smaller images are not upscaled. Target format is inferred from the extension of $target.

Parameters:
- `$source` (`string`, required): Source image path.
- `$target` (`string`, required): Destination image path (.jpg, .jpeg, .png, .gif, .webp); overwritten.
- `$maxWidth` (`int`, required): Maximum width.
- `$maxHeight` (`int`, required): Maximum height.
- `$quality` (`int`, default `85`): JPEG/WebP quality (0-100).

Returns `array{width: int, height: int}`: Resulting dimensions.

Throws:
- `InvalidArgumentException`: On invalid parameters.
- `UnexpectedValueException`: If the source is not a valid image.
- `RuntimeException`: If the image cannot be processed or saved.

### thumbnail()

```php
public static function thumbnail(string $source, string $target, int $width, int $height, int $quality = 85): void
```

Creates a thumbnail of exactly $width x $height: the image is scaled to cover the area and center-cropped (like "object-fit: cover").

Parameters:
- `$source` (`string`, required): Source image path.
- `$target` (`string`, required): Destination image path (.jpg, .jpeg, .png, .gif, .webp); overwritten.
- `$width` (`int`, required): Exact width.
- `$height` (`int`, required): Exact height.
- `$quality` (`int`, default `85`): JPEG/WebP quality (0-100).

Throws:
- `InvalidArgumentException`: On invalid parameters.
- `UnexpectedValueException`: If the source is not a valid image.
- `RuntimeException`: If the image cannot be processed or saved.

# Ini

> Strict .ini file parser with line-accurate error reporting and no implicit type coercion.

Canonical: https://foundry.insightdevhub.ro/docs/ini/  
Namespace: `Foundry\Ini` · File: `Ini.php` · Version 1.1 · PHP 8.3+

INI file parsing with clear error reporting and predictable value conversions.

Natively, parse_ini_*() returns false with a warning on syntax errors, and in default mode (INI_SCANNER_NORMAL) "yes" becomes "1", "null" becomes "", and values matching defined PHP constant names are replaced with the constant's value.

## Modes

- default (raw):   all values remain strings, exactly as in the file; double quotes are stripped, single quotes remain part of the value
- typed: true:     "true"/"yes"/"on" -> true, "false"/"no"/"off"/"none" -> false, "null" -> null, numeric strings -> int/float (INI_SCANNER_TYPED); PHP constants, ${ENV} variables and expressions ("E_ALL & ~E_NOTICE", "a|b") are rejected with an exception instead of being silently substituted or evaluated.

UTF-8 BOM is stripped (otherwise the first key would include it). Duplicate keys are permitted by PHP; last occurrence takes precedence.

## Usage

```php
require_once 'Ini.php';
use Foundry\Ini;

$config = Ini::parseFile(__DIR__.'/config.ini', sections: true);
$host = $config['database']['host'];

$flags = Ini::parseString("debug = yes\nport = 8080", typed: true);   // ['debug' => true, 'port' => 8080]
```

## Installation

```php
require_once __DIR__.'/lib/Utilities/Ini.php';

use Foundry\Ini;
```

## Methods

### parseFile()

```php
public static function parseFile(string $path, bool $sections = false, bool $typed = false): array
```

Reads and parses an INI file.

Parameters:
- `$path` (`string`, required): The file path.
- `$sections` (`bool`, default `false`): true: results are grouped by section ([section]).
- `$typed` (`bool`, default `false`): true: converts values to bool/null/int/float; false: strings only.

Returns `array<array-key, mixed>`.

Throws:
- `RuntimeException`: If the file does not exist or cannot be read.
- `UnexpectedValueException`: On syntax errors.

### parseString()

```php
public static function parseString(string $content, bool $sections = false, bool $typed = false): array
```

Parses an INI string.

Parameters:
- `$content` (`string`, required): The INI content.
- `$sections` (`bool`, default `false`): true: results are grouped by section ([section]).
- `$typed` (`bool`, default `false`): true: converts values to bool/null/int/float; false: strings only.

Returns `array<array-key, mixed>`.

Throws:
- `UnexpectedValueException`: On syntax errors.

# Base64

> Strict decoding, URL-safe Base64 (RFC 4648), hex conversion.

Canonical: https://foundry.insightdevhub.ro/docs/base64/  
Namespace: `Foundry\Base64` · File: `Base64.php` · Version 1.1 · PHP 8.3+

Base64 (standard and URL-safe) and hexadecimal encoding/decoding with strict validation.

Natively, base64_decode() without $strict accepts any text and returns corrupted data, while hex2bin() returns false with a warning. Here, invalid data throws an exception.

decode() accepts whitespace and newlines (MIME Base64 split across lines) as well as omitted "=" padding. Error messages include the data length rather than the raw data itself (which may contain tokens or keys).

## Usage

```php
require_once 'Base64.php';
use Foundry\Base64;

$pdf = Base64::decode($request['document']);      // throws an exception if not valid Base64
$token = Base64::encodeUrl(random_bytes(32));     // for URLs and JWTs: without + / =
$hash = Base64::fromHex('a1b2c3');
```

## Installation

```php
require_once __DIR__.'/lib/Utilities/Base64.php';

use Foundry\Base64;
```

## Methods

### encode()


Encodes data in standard Base64 (RFC 4648) with padding.

Parameters:
- `$data` (`string`, required)

Returns `string`.

### decode()

```php
public static function decode(string $encoded): string
```

Decodes standard Base64. Whitespace, newlines, and missing padding are accepted.

Parameters:
- `$encoded` (`string`, required)

Returns `string`.

Throws:
- `UnexpectedValueException`: If the string contains characters outside the Base64 alphabet or invalid padding.

### isValid()

```php
public static function isValid(string $encoded): bool
```

Checks whether the string is valid Base64 without throwing an exception.

Parameters:
- `$encoded` (`string`, required)

Returns `bool`.

### encodeUrl()

```php
public static function encodeUrl(string $data): string
```

Encodes data in URL-safe Base64 (RFC 4648 section 5): "-" and "_" instead of "+" and "/", without "=". Suitable for URLs, filenames, and JWTs.

Parameters:
- `$data` (`string`, required)

Returns `string`.

### decodeUrl()

```php
public static function decodeUrl(string $encoded): string
```

Decodes URL-safe Base64. The "=" padding is optional.

Parameters:
- `$encoded` (`string`, required)

Returns `string`.

Throws:
- `UnexpectedValueException`: If the string is not valid URL-safe Base64 (including if it uses the standard alphabet with "+" or "/").

### toHex()

```php
public static function toHex(string $data): string
```

Encodes data as lowercase hexadecimal text.

Parameters:
- `$data` (`string`, required)

Returns `string`.

### fromHex()

```php
public static function fromHex(string $hex): string
```

Decodes hexadecimal text (uppercase or lowercase).

Parameters:
- `$hex` (`string`, required)

Returns `string`.

Throws:
- `UnexpectedValueException`: If the string has an odd length or contains non-hexadecimal characters.

# Serializer

> Secure unserialize wrapper disabling arbitrary class instantiation and enforcing max_depth; prefer Json for new data.

Canonical: https://foundry.insightdevhub.ro/docs/serializer/  
Namespace: `Foundry\Serializer` · File: `Serializer.php` · Version 1.0 · PHP 8.3+

Secure serialize() and unserialize(). For new data, prefer Json: it is portable and cannot instantiate objects. Serializer is intended for existing data (sessions, cache, legacy columns).

## Native issues resolved

- unserialize() on untrusted data can instantiate arbitrary classes (object injection); here, by default NO classes are allowed, and permitted classes must be explicitly provided
- disallowed classes silently become __PHP_Incomplete_Class; here, an exception is thrown
- invalid data or trailing data ("Extra data") only emits a warning; here, an exception is thrown
- serialize() silently converts resources (file handles, connections) to 0; here, an exception is thrown.

## Usage

```php
require_once 'Serializer.php';
use Foundry\Serializer;

$data = Serializer::unserialize($row['payload']);                         // scalars and arrays only
$dto = Serializer::unserialize($cached, allowedClasses: [Factura::class]);  // plus permitted classes
$text = Serializer::serialize($data);
```

## Installation

```php
require_once __DIR__.'/lib/Utilities/Serializer.php';

use Foundry\Serializer;
```

## Constants

| Constant | Type | Value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `DEPTH` | `int` | `64` | Default maximum depth for unserialize(). |

## Methods

### serialize()

```php
public static function serialize(mixed $value): string
```

Serializes a value.

Parameters:
- `$value` (`mixed`, required)

Returns `string`.

Throws:
- `InvalidArgumentException`: If the value contains resources, closures, or other non-serializable values.

### unserialize()

```php
public static function unserialize(string $data, array $allowedClasses = [], int $maxDepth = self::DEPTH): mixed
```

Unserializes data. By default, no classes are allowed.

Parameters:
- `$data` (`string`, required): The serialized string.
- `$allowedClasses` (`list<class-string>`, default `[]`): Classes allowed to be instantiated.
- `$maxDepth` (`int`, default `self::DEPTH`): Maximum depth of the data structure.

Returns `mixed`: The unserialized value.

Throws:
- `UnexpectedValueException`: If the data is invalid, contains trailing data, or contains a disallowed class.
